evidence.shows: payments-api 500s appear suddenly in the latest point (3.44/s) while 201s fall, which confirms the alert's symptom.
payments-api was redeployed at 06:55:25, about 1 minute before the 500s, with REFUND_CONNECTION=kept. Every other service was created at 06:53:59 and has not changed since.
The errors on POST /payments are all psycopg_pool PoolTimeout: the database connection pool is exhausted.
A failed POST /payments spends about 5 s between its Redis idempotency SET and EVAL with no DB span, then returns 500 PoolTimeout. That gap is waiting for a pool connection.
Many POST /payments/{id}/refunds requests take 5 to 7.7 s, starting from about 06:55:53, shortly after the deploy.
A refund also fails with PoolTimeout after 7.7 s, so the pool starvation affects refunds as well.
payments-api's calls to the provider stay fast (p95 about 5 ms), so the provider is not the cause and connections are not being held across slow provider calls.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its settings from before the 06:55:25 deploy, most likely restoring the previous REFUND_CONNECTION behaviour. Recreating the container also releases any leaked connections. Afterwards, watch the 5xx rate and latency of POST /payments and refunds. Run the money check to confirm that refunds which failed with 500s did not leave our records and the provider's out of step.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so in-flight payment and refund requests fail and clients must retry. Idempotency keys in Redis should prevent double charges on those retries. If the previous settings had their own defect, it returns. Refunds that already hit the provider but errored on our side are not repaired by the rollback.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy payments-api with the current settings (REFUND_CONNECTION=kept, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents). If the pool still exhausts after the rollback, look elsewhere: check PostgreSQL connection counts and max_connections, and look for long-running transactions.
